The first quote ( the automated one, on their website) quoted $456 (estimated under 900 sq ft with 1 medium shower)
When I phoned to book, and actually spoke to someone, the quote was $778
I understand that that was based on more specific information, but was still surprised at huge increase
When the technician arrived, he looked around and said it was under 500 sq ft and would cost $950!!
When I showed him the previous quotes, he agreed to $778
The actual charge , on completion was$749 I have no idea how that number was arrived at.
Be sure you are very attentive to the charges!!

reviews.comment:
I’ve used Brimleys twice for move out/cleaning. Both times, the value for the work done has been great, overall I’m very happy with the fact that I get the quoted price without surprises on site for extra charges.
However, this last time I had a VERY severe stain/damage issue with carpet. Because the carpet was warrantied against stains, I wanted to try to get anything that would come out, out, so that we could evaluate for the warranty (we had to attempt to clean it first!)
To be honest, I had very low expectations because the damage was so bad.
My tech Nick was great, he was on time, positive, and fairly optimistic about getting at least some of the damage out. He was also very nice, worked hard and was helpful with information about the cleaning.
The process doesn’t take too long, the carpets dry fairly quickly, and above all-a good deal of the staining and dirt came out.
Now, this situation is above and beyond what most normal staining should look like. If this had been “normal” wear and tear/staining, I’m sure these carpets would look brand new. However-Brimleys far exceeded my expectations on getting it to any level of clean, and actually got it to what might be considered a normal amount of clean!
I will absolutely continue to use and recommend Brimleys for our carpet cleaning needs!

reviews.comment:
I have had great experiences with any Chem-dry but I have been really disappointed this past visit (they came a couple months ago).

The technicians were kind, professional, and on time.  I walked them though the house and pointed out a few areas that needed extra attention.  One spot was a spot that had a urine smell (it wasn't super strong but I knew it was there).  I asked that they give extra attention to it (they never mentioned any extra urine treatment).

They cleaned in a timely manner and left.  Afterwards I went to smell the urine spot and it still had an oder.  A day or so late they followed up (love how professional this is) and asked how everything went.  I shared my disappointment and they said they would schedule someone to come back out.  Great!   I couldn't be home for the second cleaning so my husband worked from home in order to be there.

When I came home the second cleaning had done a special "urine treatment" (that was never mentioned in the first cleaning and they charged us an additional $75 for the cleaning of a small area).  The house smelled so strong of chemicals, but was told the smell would die down as soon as it dried.  It took weeks for the chemical smell to go away, but now (months later) the urine smell is even stronger and constant in the room.

I spent between $500-600 for this cleaning (they cleaned my leather sectional which was $200-250 alone) and our house is less than 1600sq feet with all carpet upstairs.  I know I could have paid less for the same type of service.

I'm just sharing our experience.  I hope anyone who reads this has a better experience.

reviews.comment: The cleaning didn’t appear to be any better or any worse than others I have had for 1/3 the price. reviews.comment:
After waiting 4 months and exerting pressure on Brimley’s corporate office and other on-line review sites, I finally received a check for a little over $5200 for the replacement of our sofa-sectional that they ruined beyond repair.  If they had taken responsibility upfront for their technician’s incompetence instead of blaming the stains on my wife’s dirty calves, I would have been satisfied.

Since filing my initial review on Brimley's White Glove Chem-Dry, several things have changed which I wanted to clarify, especially regarding the rebuttal from the owner of Brimleys, Michael Court. Their company has sent out 3 different technicians to clean & re-clean our sofa-sectional. According to Brimley’s general manager JoAnn Talbot, the 3rd technician that came out was their expert & #1 corporate trainer. Prior to him re-cleaning the sofa-sectional he claimed that the sofa stains were caused from my wife’s dirty calf’s. To add further insult both he & the general manager said the lighting in our room made the sofa appear to have stains. Afterwards their general manager emailed me and said our sofa was cleaned and cleaned properly.
Since this ordeal, I have received feedback from three professionals regarding the condition of the sofa-sectional and they have all been unanimous in their opinion. After inspecting the sectional an independent insurance adjuster (approved by many major insurance companies) provided me a written statement indicating the sectional was ruined beyond repair because of improper cleaning and/or improper chemical balance. After reviewing detailed pictures, I received verbal confirmation from a senior customer service representative with Williams Sonoma (owner of the Pottery Barn from where we purchased the sofa) indicating the same conclusion.  I also had Mr. JR Ordonez, owner of Customers Own Fabric, an upholstering store, fiscally inspect the sofa. He too indicated the same.
Mr. Court indicated that I refused to allow them to clean the sofa a 4th time and he’s right. After cleaning it twice, they sent out their expert technician for a third cleaning. Cleaning the sofa a fourth time is a waste of my time especially when the sofa was ruined beyond repair by their first ill trained technician.
Mr. Court also indicated I signed a disclaimer that basically lets them off the hook in situations like this. I was never required to sign or initial any of these areas and my original copy will indicate this.
A couple of weeks ago I requested Mr. Court file a claim with their insurance company. He replied that he would file a claim only if I removed the negative review first. Since then he indicated he did file a claim but wasn’t sure when he did it. It’s been over a week and I have not heard from their insurance adjustor. I just read his rebuttal yesterday and it became obvious to me that Mr. Court has been misleading me with his intentions or resolving my complaint, nor do  think he ever intended to file a insurance claim. I honestly believe Mr. Court felt his disingenuous rebuttal would be sufficient in insuring doing business with potential customers.
According to the Pottery Barn, the cost to replace our ruined sofa-sectional is approximately $5200 and their offer to reimburse us $160 for the cleaning is an insult my intelligence. Throughout this horrific process their employees have been offensive, unprofessional and have exhibited an extreme lack of follow up. Ironically, I have contracted with their firm twice before with great success. Obviously the professionalism and integrity I experienced before no longer exists. I would not recommend this company to anyone to do any type of cleaning especially if you value your carpeting and furniture.

reviewReply.comment:
Mr. Abernathy, we regret that you were not satisfied with our services. We strive to do our best job cleaning with the best equipment and well-trained employees to service our customers. We have returned several times and are willing to return again for additional treatments, but you refuse, so we will honor our guarantee and refund you the full amount of your upholstery cleaning. We do not feel it fair for us to purchase a new sofa.

We do have all of our customers sign a disclaimer because of so many potential issues that can come up when attempting to clean furniture. We rarely see issues like this, but we want to make customers aware that they are possible. Manufactures don't always design their furniture with the understanding that it will need to be cleaned, so fabrics, cushions, and backings can have adverse affects when being attempted to clean. Although we don't know what the issue is in this situation, it appears to me to be a PH imbalance that could be corrected with an acidic treatment. It doesn't appear to be because of any chemical we use, or burning with "too hot" water (we offer steam cleaning services, so the water will necessarily be hot).

I have apologized and will apologize again that our technicians made a guess as to what was causing the issue. They did not do it to insult, just to attempt to understand the issue. We pride ourselves on delivering great customer service and getting great reviews, so we are saddened that the situation has come to this.

Thank you for your past business and we wish you the best in the future.

reviews.comment: Very nice people but very expensive for the work needed and not very thorough.  I was charged for a full room when only parts of the carpet were actually cleaned.  I am not even sure that I was really given the stain protection since my rug was so saturated with pet odor stuff that it took 3 days to dry and I question if a stain protector could be applied on such a wet surface.  Also, when all was said and done I still do not feel that my rug is odor free.

reviewReply.comment: Sorry for any confusion, Debbie, we try to explain everything and be thorough and detailed in both our service and communication. Dave, our trainer, is one of the very best at that as is Sean (both of your techs that day). When treating for pet urine, it IS necessary to saturate the area to get all the way to the source of the urine odor. We can't just treat the surface carpet fibers because you'd still have odor coming from the urine in the carpet's backing and pad and that would be a disservice. As for thorough assessment, Dave even used a tarp and got on his belly underneath it to ensure the best success at locating spots with odor to address your concerns to the fullest. Because there was such extensive odor, he actually used more treatments than you were charged for (twice as many actually) to be sure to address your greatest concern and keep the price at your comfort level. We also indicated several times that we'd be more than happy to come back out once the treated areas were completely dry (need to let the odor treatment completely work it's magic) if you weren't satisfied or still had odor remaining. We stand by our work completely! Dave does all he can at every job to ensure customer satisfaction. We do measure the room wall to wall; our formula accounts for it being a furnished room-large pieces like desks are not moved. The charge for that 1 room was $69 to clean. That would have been the sum total of your charge if you just wanted the carpet cleaned. The additional costs you chose were for the sanitizing & protecting as well as the odor treatment plus a large area rug. I'm sorry if the protectant wasn't explained completely to you - it is co-applied at the time of cleaning to give you the greatest protection - 1) it gets on the entire carpet fiber (rather than other products just sprayed on the tips of the fibers); and 2) it bonds to the fibers better as the solution coming off the truck is over 200 degrees. It's the closest thing to factory protection that you can get so, rest assured, you are well covered :) We would be pleased if you would accept the offer we extended to come back out if you weren't thrilled with the service or results! I know it's never convenient to have people come back but we really do want to get it right and we'll find a day and time that works best for you. Thank you - JoAnn / 602.753.2776

reviews.comment: Brimley's White Glove Chem-Dry cleaned 3 rooms of carpet for us (467 sq. feet), and significantly lightened the traffic area paths.  Our main problem was small dog urine areas, however, we chose the Healthy Home Premium Service over the Stain Fighter Service, since it includes "stain fighter services plus professional strength deodorizer / sanitizer to reduce unhealthy bacteria."  While the urine stains are mostly gone, the smell remains and is particularly noticeable when the weather was more humid / wet.  Apparently, to get rid of any smell, we would have had to added $259 for the Stain Fighter Service in addition to the $304 for the Health Home Premium Service, which is advertised to include the Stain Fighter Service.  For us (retirees), the cost of Brimley's carpet cleaning services was quite expensive, especially for the relatively small areas of carpeting that were cleaned and since our doggie urine smell problem still remains.  Surely there is a quality carpet cleaning service out there somewhere who can address the dirt / urine problems at a reasonable cost.  I'll keep looking.  FYI:  The service crew member who cleaned our carpets (Ryan) was very professional, courteous, and polite, which was certainly appreciated.

reviewReply.comment: Hi, Jan. I'm sorry we couldn't speak directly about your concerns so I could explain any mis-communication or confusion about service packages and the pricing. If you still want to return my call, that'd be great! We want to be clear and we want you to be happy. The $259 was for the clean & protect service and the $304 Healthy Home you chose DOES include the protectant. Your tech simply listed the price for both options. The package you chose does sound like a good one for you (I like to protect and sanitize always even though I blame it on the extra paw traffic). When you scheduled the appointment, Michael discussed your concerns including the option of Pet Urine Removal Treatment (PURT) which is an extensive treatment that addresses odor concerns in the carpet, backing and pad. Because urine is liquid it goes into the backing and pad which regular cleaning of the carpet fibers doesn't address, nor would sanitizing eliminate that odor. Since your stated concern was related to the stains and you declined by signature the P.U.R.T. treatment to treat for odor acknowledging that you were "offered and informed about the P.U.R.T. treatment. I understand that without P.U.R.T., urine odor has not been treated." it seems like we provided the service based on your needs and desires. If you do feel now, that you'd like to address the odor, we can still do that! It's not uncommon for people to treat for odor and then clean or visa versa. We do try our very best to provide services based on our customer's needs, desires and budgets so I apologize if we were unclear in any way. -- JoAnn
